anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.text:
The ticket repair is saved and verified: acme/widgets#77 now reads "The report-view setting uses the shared settings resolver." That row is `in-scope` as written. It matches the path already traced, from the defaults owned at `settings/resolver.ts:12` to the consumer at `ui/report-view.ts:30`, so it needs no disposition and no new boundary. The framing stays as you kept it.

One behavior is still open: what the report view does with active filters when you switch workspaces. Today they carry over and can hide rows in the new workspace. Which outcome should the resolver-backed setting produce?

A) Reset on switch by default - the setting defaults to clearing filters on a workspace change, and users can opt into keeping them.
B) Keep on switch by default - current behavior stays the default, and users can opt into reset.
C) Remember per workspace - each workspace restores its own last filters, so nothing carries across.
D) other - name it

Recommendation: A - the reported defect is carried-over filters hiding rows, so a reset default fixes it for everyone, while the resolver default keeps one read path and lets users opt back in.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.text:
The repaired criterion in acme/widgets#77 now requires the shared settings resolver, so it remains **in-scope** and matches the verified resolver-to-report-view path.

What should happen to report filters when the workspace changes?
A) Clear the filters so the new workspace starts unfiltered.
B) Restore each workspace’s previously used filters.
C) Keep the current filters across workspaces.
D) Other - name it.
Recommendation: A - it directly prevents filters from silently hiding rows in the new workspace without introducing per-workspace persistence.
